vopros: Who in the US sets up a voice AI assistant that answers customer calls in Russian?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Several companies and platforms offer voice AI assistants that can answer customer calls in Russian, and businesses in the US can set these up on their own through self-service platforms. Here's an overview of the main options:

## Self-Service Voice AI Platforms (No Coding Required)

**VoiceGenie** offers a dedicated Russian voice AI product where you can "launch your Russian Voice AI campaigns in minutes — without any technical setup or coding." It can switch between Russian, Uzbek, and English in the same call, which is useful for multilingual customer bases. It's powered by ElevenLabs technology, delivering expressive, native-sounding speech.

**OpenMic.ai** is described as "a leading voice AI platform that enables businesses to build sophisticated Russian-speaking voice agents for customer service, sales, and support automation," with advanced Russian language processing that supports standard Russian and regional variations from Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, and other Russian-speaking regions.

**Retell AI** supports 31+ languages out of the box, piping transcripts through GPT-4-class models to translate and generate native responses in milliseconds, and its auto language detection can switch to 10+ languages including Russian. It also offers a no-code drag-and-drop builder plus robust SDKs that integrate with Twilio, Vonage, SIP trunks, and CRMs.

**HighLevel (GoHighLevel)** includes Russian among its supported languages for Voice AI Agents, alongside English, German, Spanish, French, Portuguese, and dozens of others. Setup involves logging into your account, going to AI Agents, and selecting the desired language from the Language option.

**Zadarma** launched an AI voice assistant that is deeply integrated with its own cloud PBX (VoIP system) and CRM platform, supporting eight major languages including English, Chinese, Spanish, French, German, Russian, Portuguese, and Arabic. Setup is straightforward: connect the Zadarma cloud PBX, go to AI Studio → Agents to create a voice AI assistant, then choose the language, model, and voice.

## Enterprise CX Platforms

**ServiceNow's AI Voice Agents** support 18+ languages and dialects globally, including Russian, Arabic, Portuguese, Dutch, French, German, Hindi, and more, with the ability to assign a primary language and several secondary languages, prompting callers to select their preferred language at the start of a call.

**Zendesk** offers configurable multi-language AI agents where you can route callers to the right language based on phone number, caller info, or preference, using region-appropriate terms — fully generative, with no need to translate procedures or dialogues. Customers can even request to switch languages mid-conversation, and the AI will detect the request and switch to it if supported.

## Underlying Voice Technology

If you're building a custom solution rather than using an off-the-shelf platform, **Soniox** provides Russian speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and translation through a single API, reducing integration complexity for building Russian voice products, while **ElevenLabs** offers high-quality Russian text-to-speech with clear, engaging audio, including voices tailored for local business etiquette and clear communication.

---

**Bottom line:** For a US-based business, the fastest path is typically a no-code platform like **VoiceGenie, OpenMic.ai, Retell AI, HighLevel, or Zadarma** — you sign up, select Russian as a language, connect your phone number/CRM, and the AI agent starts answering calls. If you need deeper customization, pairing an LLM with APIs like **Soniox** (speech-to-text) and **ElevenLabs** (text-to-speech) lets you build a fully custom Russian-language phone agent.
